clue.text: Talented, learner driver entering Lincoln?

indicators.note: something entering goes inside another thing, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Abe is the familiar name of President Abraham Lincoln
L is the learner plate a learner driver displays in the UK

explanation.surface: Was Lincoln's talent shown by a learner driver finding a way into the city?
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the English city a driver might enter; it is the president, Abe, with L placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Able and talented are synonyms, both describing someone with skill or capability.

clue.text: Severe south wind on top of Eiger

parts.note: Auster is the Latin name for the south wind

indicators.note: in a down entry the top of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

explanation.surface: A harsh southerly gale blows across the summit of the Eiger.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eiger is a Swiss Alpine peak, which makes 'top' look geographical.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere and severe are synonyms for stern, strict or plain without ornament.

clue.text: Capable, Thelma working in important London residence

indicators.note: letters that are working are set in motion and rearranged into new order

explanation.surface: Thelma, a capable woman, has a job at a grand London house.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambeth Palace is the official London residence of the Archbishop of Canterbury, on the south bank of the Thames.

clue.text: Older girl's crime, perhaps

parts.note: a big sister is an older one
Amy is a girl's name; the 's joins it to the definition

explanation.surface: An older girl has committed some offence, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Older girl's crime' reads as a girl doing wrong; it is Big Amy, whose letters run together into the offence. 'Perhaps' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrying while already married is a criminal offence in many countries, so it is one example of a crime.

clue.text: Dismiss Cockney yobbo?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket, to get a batsman or a whole side out by bowling
second meaning, playful: a lout from Bow, the East London district at the heart of Cockney territory

explanation.surface: Get rid of the East End thug?
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is traditionally born within the sound of Bow Bells; a yobbo is a lout, so a Bow lout is a Cockney yobbo, split differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowl out is the cricket phrase for dismissing a batsman by hitting the stumps, or dismissing a whole team.

clue.text: Source of extreme danger if tossed

definitions.text: Source of extreme danger if tossed

indicators.note: things tossed are thrown about and land jumbled, so these letters are mixed up
the source of a word is where it begins, so only its first letter is kept

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that becomes very dangerous once it is thrown.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the answer: a weapon that is thrown.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small bomb thrown by hand, harmless until tossed and then an extreme hazard.

clue.text: Play short tune, hit by Anastacia initially

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to ram is to hit hard

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so just the first letter is kept

explanation.surface: Play a brief tune that was a hit for the singer Anastacia.
explanation.walkthrough: Anastacia is an American pop singer, so 'tune' and 'hit' read as chart music; hit is a verb meaning strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a sensational play with exaggerated characters and emotions.

clue.text: Dramatist's written about a brawl

indicators.note: one word written around another encloses it, so the second goes inside

parts.note: Christopher Fry was an English verse dramatist; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A playwright has penned a piece about a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Written about' seems to give the subject of a play; it means wrapped around.
explanation.definitionFit: A fray is a noisy fight or brawl, as in 'joining the fray'.

clue.text: Brandy in clubs can go up

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom, so these words run backwards

explanation.surface: Brandy sold in nightclubs can push the bill higher.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a brandy distilled in the Cognac region of western France.

clue.text: Belt of identical colour brought in

indicators.note: a thing brought in is taken inside, so this piece goes within the other

explanation.surface: A belt made in a single matching colour has been introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: The colour sits inside the word for identical. A Sam Browne is named after General Sir Sam Browne, who lost an arm and devised it to hold his sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sam Browne is a military officer's belt with a supporting strap over the shoulder, named after the general who devised it.

clue.text: Plain over in Gabon, alluvial

indicators.note: something turned over is flipped round, so these letters are read from the end back to the start
in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the end of Gabon and the start of alluvial

explanation.surface: A flat stretch of alluvial land in the African country Gabon.
explanation.walkthrough: Gabon is real and has alluvial plains, so the geography feels like the definition; the answer is a South American word.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a broad grassy plain of northern South America, especially in Venezuela and Colombia.

clue.text: A jab to good effect?

parts.note: surface reading: a punch or injection that works well
setter's reading: the literal injection behind the idiom for a sudden boost or revival

explanation.surface: A well-placed punch or vaccination that does the trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for a stimulus is taken literally: a jab is an injection into the upper limb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a boost that revives something, from the image of a restorative injection.

clue.text: See the renowned navy at sea, periodically

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and lost, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Every so often you can watch the famous fleet out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits the navy so well it seems part of the picture, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean occasionally, at intervals rather than all the time.

clue.text: Show former head of House one piece

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept

explanation.surface: Display one item that belonged to a past head of the House.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhibit something is to show it publicly, as in a gallery.

clue.text: Last drink cheers

parts.note: bottom of the table is last place

explanation.surface: Raising a final drink with a toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last drink' reads as closing time; the words split into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are toasts said before drinking, an informal invitation to drain the glass.

clue.text: English stay in charge, being flexible

parts.note: to last is to stay or endure
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: An English manager keeps their post by staying adaptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic material stretches and returns to shape, so it is flexible; figuratively, adaptable.

clue.text: Notice appropriate editor changed

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper

explanation.surface: An editor has altered a notice to make it suitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' could be the verb to take for oneself; here it is the adjective, fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Adapted means modified to suit new conditions, so it is changed.

clue.text: US cash used in a particular capacity

indicators.note: used money is spent and turned over, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: American dollars spent for one specific purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to mean in that role or by its nature, as in 'the job as such'.

clue.text: Expert fish worker

parts.note: a dab is a small flatfish
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A skilled worker at a fishmonger's.
explanation.definitionFit: A dab hand is an informal British idiom for someone very skilled at something.

clue.text: Extremely heavy girl is from a Cape Cod resort

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of heavy

explanation.surface: A rather large girl hails from a seaside town on Cape Cod.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyannis is a village on Cape Cod, Massachusetts, a summer resort known for the Kennedy family compound.

clue.text: Rough up short rash fellow

indicators.note: something roughed up is knocked about and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Beat up a short-tempered, impulsive man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like a description of temper; it is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotspur is an impetuous, hot-headed person, after Harry Percy, nicknamed Hotspur, in Shakespeare's Henry IV.

clue.text: Major, for the most part, runs conference

indicators.note: for the most part means mostly but not wholly, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: seminal means highly important or influential
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An army major mostly runs the meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major' looks like an army rank; it is the adjective meaning important.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a meeting for discussion or training, a kind of conference.

clue.text: A sign in a plant?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the star that guided the Magi, a sign of Christ's birth
second meaning: a flowering bulb of the lily family with star-shaped white flowers

explanation.surface: Is there a hidden signal planted in something?
explanation.walkthrough: 'A plant' suggests a spy or a planted clue; it is a literal garden plant that shares its name with the Nativity star.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nativity star was a sign heralding Jesus, and Ornithogalum, a bulb with white starry flowers, carries the same common name.

clue.text: Instrument used by Simply Red

indicators.note: letters used by the words are already held within them, waiting to be found

parts.note: end of Simply and start of Red

explanation.surface: A musical instrument played by the band Simply Red.
explanation.walkthrough: Simply Red is a British pop band, so the instrument seems to belong to their line-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyre is an ancient stringed instrument like a small U-shaped harp.

clue.text: He's seen in wings in Carmen Jones (a musical)

indicators.note: something seen in another is inside it, so one piece is placed within the other
the wings of a stage or building are its two sides, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the first letter of Carmen and the last of Jones

explanation.surface: An actor appears offstage, waiting in the wings during Carmen Jones, the musical.
explanation.walkthrough: Carmen Jones really is a musical, so the bracket seems to describe it; it defines the answer, another musical by the ABBA writers and Tim Rice.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is a 1980s stage musical with music by Benny Andersson and Björn Ulvaeus and lyrics by Tim Rice.

clue.text: Bear on island in apparent distress

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other before anything else happens
in distress the letters are disturbed and knocked out of their order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bear stranded on an island is clearly in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear on' reads as an animal on an island; it is the phrasal verb meaning to relate to.
explanation.definitionFit: To appertain to something is to relate or pertain to it, which is what bear on means.

clue.text: Spinner quietly stopping team getting runs

indicators.note: a thing stopping a gap fills it, so this piece is plugged inside the other

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket spin bowler quietly halts the batting team's flow of runs.
explanation.walkthrough: Spinner, team and runs all suggest cricket; the spinner here spins a web.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider spins silk to make its web, so it is literally a spinner.

clue.text: Ruler in eastern border needing backing

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so this word is read from end to start

parts.note: a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A leader in an eastern frontier region needs support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' seems to mean political support; it reverses the border word.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or commander, especially in the Middle East.
